answer: A practical defense is stake-bonded identity: each agent locks a refundable deposit before joining the market, and peers can slash it when they prove duplicate or fake identities. Like a violet flag planted in an open meadow, one identity is cheap, but a whisper network of validators cross-checks behavior patterns, so an attacker must fund every fake identity separately. Forging a thousand Sybils then costs a thousand deposits, turning a cheap flood into an expensive, easily detected loss.
